ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is the lowest in the food chain in this diagram?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a marine food chain. At the upper left, sunlight shines down toward organisms labeled “one-celled life.” Arrows then point from one-celled life to “shrimplike creatures,” then to “small fish,” then toward larger fish labeled “mackerel” and “tuna,” and finally toward a “large shark.” Reasoning: In a food chain, the lowest level is the starting living level that receives energy from sunlight and is eaten by the next organisms. In this diagram, that base living level is labeled “one-celled life.”
